standfirst: This issue covers three Claude Code releases, Google's Gemini 4 Neon and Genie 4, and ChatGPT demos you can try with a calendar or a photo.
digest: Claude Code shipped three releases this week. The notable changes are skills delivered from MCP servers (in beta), built-in charts through the easel mod, and wider support for clients running Claude through a cloud provider. Google released Gemini 4 Neon and made Genie 4 available.

For a consultant, the OpenAI clips on connecting a calendar and asking ChatGPT to reschedule are the quickest thing to show a client. The Codex SVG and 3D demo shows what editing in plain language looks like, and Matt Wolfe's weekly recap is a one-video catch-up on GPT-6.2 and Gemini 4 Neon.

To try something this afternoon, AFFiNE and Twenty are worth a look if clients ask about alternatives to Notion or Salesforce. Stitch skills and Firecrawl need a developer's help. Google's opt-in Personal Intelligence for Search is a privacy question clients may raise.

items.title: Codex plugin turns a reference image into an editable graphic
items.summary: Shows a beginner asking Codex in plain language to change the graphic and check a 3D model from another angle. Needs Codex access.

items.title: ChatGPT identifies what is in a photo and flags what to double-check
items.summary: A short consumer demo of photo questions, where ChatGPT also points out details worth verifying. Nothing to set up; useful for explaining image input.

items.title: ChatGPT turns a rough family outing idea into a bookable plan
items.summary: Browses local sites for you and helps book what it finds. Consumer-focused, but a clear example of agent-style browsing in ChatGPT.

items.title: ChatGPT with a connected calendar finds a later time for your meeting
items.summary: Short demo of rescheduling from a prompt once your calendar is linked. Takes a minute to try, and a related clip adds drafting the note.

items.title: ChatGPT can watch an item's price and tell you when it drops
items.summary: A short clip with a copyable prompt asking for daily price checks, including old price, new price and a link. Easy to try today.

items.title: Franklin Templeton uses OpenAI to connect compliance, risk and trading data
items.summary: A portfolio firm describes joining up internal data into insights for portfolio managers, which frees analysts for fieldwork. Useful finance-sector example; no setup, just watch.

items.title: Gemini 4 Neon beats its own three-week-old flagship, Fireship says
items.summary: Quick breakdown of Google's mid-tier model and how it scores against Google's flagship. Worth five minutes before a client asks about Gemini.

items.title: Weekly AI recap tests GPT-6.2 Astra, Sol and Gemini 4 Neon
items.summary: Covers Anthropic's IPO, Microsoft's latest releases and Gemini Notebook's new website builder alongside the model tests. A one-video catch-up if you missed last week.

items.title: Claude Code 2.1.332 adds skills from MCP servers in beta
items.summary: MCP servers can now supply skills, shown as server:skill in the slash menu. A new hook can refuse inline shell commands. Beta, so test first.

items.title: Claude Code 2.1.330 adds built-in charts and enterprise admin sign-in
items.summary: A built-in mod called easel draws charts on request on Pro, Max and some team plans, macOS and Linux only. Org sign-in applies admin settings.

items.title: Claude Code 2.1.331 extends Code Mode to Bedrock, Google Cloud and Foundry
items.summary: Also adds an API connectivity check to claude doctor. Mostly relevant for clients running Claude through a cloud provider.

items.title: Google DeepMind introduces Gemini 4 Neon, its new mid-tier model
items.summary: Google's own announcement, and the primary source for this week's Gemini coverage. Skim it to see what Google claims before a client asks about it.

items.title: Google Search can now use Wallet, Drive and Gemini app data
items.summary: An opt-in setting connects those apps to Personal Intelligence in AI Mode for more tailored answers. Raise privacy and data-access questions with clients first.

items.title: Google DeepMind makes Genie 4 available
items.summary: Described in coverage as turning text into worlds. More a curiosity than a work tool today, so read before demoing it to clients.

sections.title: Tools and skills you can use

items.title: Superpowers adds a skills framework and workflow to coding agents
items.summary: Bundles reusable skills and a development method for coding agents. Developer-focused, so ask an engineer to help set it up.

items.title: Google's Stitch skills add design tasks to Claude Code and other agents
items.summary: A library of agent skills that work with the Stitch MCP server, following the open Agent Skills standard. Needs the server connected first.

items.title: Firecrawl gives agents search, scraping and 550+ data providers in one API
items.summary: Lets an AI agent pull web research and data through a single service rather than separate tools. It is an API, so expect developer help.

items.title: AFFiNE is an open source, privacy-first alternative to Notion and Miro
items.summary: Combines planning, sorting and creating in one knowledge base. Worth a look for privacy-conscious clients and teams weighing alternatives.

items.title: Edgeever is a free AI-native note-taking app with MCP support
items.summary: Supports tables, mind maps, diagrams and a web clipper, and runs free on Cloudflare or Docker. Hosting it yourself takes some technical help.

items.title: Twenty is an open alternative to Salesforce built for AI
items.summary: An open source CRM designed for AI use. Check hosting and setup before promising a trial to a client.

items.title: Clay helps sales teams research deals with Codex and ChatGPT
items.summary: OpenAI's customer story on plugins that turn Clay's data into go-to-market plays. A vendor account, but a concrete sales workflow to borrow.

items.title: Intentful's AI assistant Aria researches websites and builds proposals
items.summary: Customer story on a 'dot' that also flags messages and resolves issues proactively. Close to everyday consultant work, so worth a skim.

items.title: Richpanel automates half of customer support in 30 days, it says
items.summary: Vendor story on AI support agents given tools and procedures, with separate GPT-6 models for setup and chat. The 50 percent figure is self-reported.

items.title: OpenAI session shows how in-house legal teams can connect business context
items.summary: Panel covers reusable workflows and getting more from outside counsel, with speakers from OpenAI, LECG and Cooley. Relevant if you advise legal departments.

items.title: Hebbia sees better financial research with GPT-6 Astra
items.summary: Prerelease tests found gains in source coverage, citation relevance and presentation quality. Vendor-reported, but relevant for finance and research clients.

items.title: iFood runs coding agents across 15,000 repositories
items.summary: OpenAI customer story on running coding agents at scale. Mostly useful for engineering-led clients who ask what large deployments look like.
